results.name: Jackson_County_Parcel_Trends
results.title: Jackson County Parcel Trends
results.description:
Jackson County Parcel Trends provides summarized historical information derived from Jackson County’s authoritative parcel and tax roll data. The resource is designed to support analysis and visualization of changes in parcel characteristics, assessed values, and property tax information over time.

Data are organized by tax year and summarized at several levels, including countywide totals, municipality, property class, and school district. Historical records are processed through an automated GIS workflow to provide consistent year-to-year reporting while accounting for records that may appear in more than one annual parcel submission.

This resource supports Jackson County’s public-facing parcel trend dashboards and related ArcGIS Hub content. It is intended for informational and planning purposes and should not be interpreted as an official tax bill, assessment notice, or accounting of revenues retained by Jackson County.

For official property assessment or taxation information, users should consult the appropriate municipal assessor, taxing jurisdiction, or Jackson County office.
results.snippet: Provides summarized historical parcel, assessment, and property tax information for Jackson County, Wisconsin, organized by tax year, municipality, property class, and school district. Designed to support public-facing parcel trend dashboards and land information resources.
results.licenseInfo:
This resource is provided by Jackson County, Wisconsin, for informational and public reference purposes. Data are derived from County parcel and tax roll records and may be subject to updates, corrections, timing differences, or other changes associated with assessment and taxation processes.

The information provided should not be considered an official tax bill, assessment notice, legal description, survey, or determination of property ownership or value. Property tax amounts shown may include levies for multiple taxing jurisdictions and should not be interpreted as revenue collected or retained solely by Jackson County.

Users should verify information with the appropriate assessor, taxing jurisdiction, or Jackson County office before relying upon it for financial, legal, or other official purposes. Jackson County assumes no liability for decisions or actions taken based upon the use of this information.

results.title: Parcels, Compiled from Opt-In Open Data Counties, Minnesota
results.description:
This dataset is a compilation of county parcel data from Minnesota counties that have opted-in for their parcel data to be included in this dataset. It includes the following 59 counties that have opted-in as of the publication date of this dataset: Aitkin County, Anoka County, Becker County, Benton County, Big Stone County, Carlton County, Carver County, Cass County, Chippewa County, Chisago County, Clay County, Clearwater County, Cook County, Crow Wing County, Dakota County, Douglas County, Fillmore County, Grant County, Hennepin County, Houston County, Isanti County, Itasca County, Jackson County, Koochiching County, Lac qui Parle County, Lake County, Lake of the Woods County, Lyon County, Marshall County, McLeod County, Mille Lacs County, Morrison County, Mower County, Murray County, Norman County, Olmsted County, Otter Tail County, Pennington County, Pipestone County, Polk County, Pope County, Ramsey County, Red Lake County, Renville County, Rice County, Scott County, Sherburne County, St. Louis County, Stearns County, Steele County, Stevens County, Traverse County, Wabasha County, Waseca County, Washington County, Wilkin County, Winona County, Wright County, and Yellow Medicine County. If you represent a county not included in this dataset and would like to opt-in, please contact Heather Albrecht (Heather.Albrecht@hennepin.us), co-chair of the Minnesota Geospatial Advisory Council (GAC)’s Parcels and Land Records Committee's Open Data Subcommittee. County parcel data does not need to be in the GAC parcel data standard to be included. MnGeo will map the county fields to the GAC standard. County parcel data records have been assembled into a single dataset with a common coordinate system (UTM Zone 15) and common attribute schema. The county parcel data attributes have been mapped to the GAC parcel data standard for Minnesota: https://www.mngeo.state.mn.us/committee/standards/parcel_attrib/parcel_attrib.html This compiled parcel dataset was created using Python code developed by Minnesota state agency GIS professionals, and represents a best effort to map individual county source file attributes into the common attribute schema of the GAC parcel data standard. The attributes from counties are mapped to the most appropriate destination column. In some cases, the county source files included attributes that were not mapped to the GAC standard. Additionally, some county attribute fields were parsed and mapped to multiple GAC standard fields, such as a single line address. Each quarter, MnGeo provides a text file to counties that shows how county fields are mapped to the GAC standard. Additionally, this text file shows the fields that are not mapped to the standard and those that are parsed. If a county shares changes to how their data should be mapped, MnGeo updates the compilation. If you represent a county and would like to update how MnGeo is mapping your county attribute fields to this compiled dataset, please contact us. This dataset is a snapshot of parcel data, and the source date of the county data may vary. Users should consult County websites to see the most up-to-date and complete parcel data. There have been recent changes in date/time fields, and their processing, introduced by our software vendor. In some cases, this has resulted in date fields being empty. We are aware of the issue and are working to correct it for future parcel data releases. THE DATA IS PROVIDED “AS IS” WITH NO GUARANTEE OR REPRESENTATION ABOUT THE ACCURACY, CURRENCY, SUITABILITY, PERFORMANCE, MECHANTABILITY, RELIABILITY OR FITINESS OF THIS DATA FOR ANY PARTICULAR PURPOSE. The distribution version of the fgdb is compressed to help reduce the data footprint. results.snippet: Parcel data has been identified as a foundational data layer for Minnesota and provides benefits for many operational uses. This dataset enables users to visualize the government owned parcels within each opt-in open county. It provides a best-effort inference of government ownership based on attributes provided by counties (often owner name, taxpayer name, or use class) where the ownership was not directly provided. This dataset was developed to enable geospatial professionals to perform statewide geospatial analysis, research, and mapping. For instance, knowing where government units have land holdings will help with coordinating land management and conservation efforts across Minnesota. The dataset provides a subset of the parcels from opt-in, open data counties, in a common coordinate system. Users can join this dataset to the open parcel dataset using the objectid field to access parcel attributes in the standard GAC schema.

results.title: Parcel Boundaries of Indiana Current
results.description: This data layer is an Esri file geodatabase polygon feature class that contains parcel boundaries maintained by county agencies in Indiana. It was released by the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO) on February 1, 2022. The IGIO compiled the data as part of the Indiana Data Harvest program between the Indiana Geographic Information Council (IGIC) and all Indiana counties to provide the most accurate framework data for the citizens of Indiana. These layers include address points, street centerlines, land parcels, and governmental boundaries.
results.snippet:
This dataset was developed to provide accurate parcel boundaries for Indiana, as part of Indiana's annual GIS Data harvest Data Sharing Initiative (IDSI) of the Indiana Geographic Information Office (IGIO).

results.title: Fire Districts in Jackson County
results.description:
The Fire District Boundaries layer represents the approximate geographic extents of fire protection districts in Jackson County, Oregon. Boundaries are intended for general reference, mapping, and spatial analysis and may not reflect legal service boundaries at a parcel-level scale.

This dataset supports planning, coordination, and public information needs related to emergency services, land use, and jurisdictional reference. Boundary locations may be updated as source data is refined or administrative changes occur.

Data Sources

  • Emergency Communications of Southern Oregon (ECSO 911)
  • Jackson County Tax Assessor's Office

Data Quality & Limitations

Fire district boundaries are compiled from authoritative local sources but are intended for cartographic and informational purposes only. Boundaries may be generalized and should not be used to determine legal jurisdiction, service eligibility, or response responsibility. For official determinations, users should contact the appropriate fire district or county agency directly.

results.snippet: Parcel data has been identified as a foundational data layer for Minnesota and provides benefits for many operational uses. This dataset enables users to visualize the government owned parcels within each opt-in open county. It provides a best-effort inference of government ownership based on attributes provided by counties (often owner name, taxpayer name, or use class) where the ownership was not directly provided. This dataset was developed to enable geospatial professionals to perform statewide geospatial analysis, research, and mapping. For instance, knowing where government units have land holdings will help with coordinating land management and conservation efforts across Minnesota. The dataset provides a subset of the parcels from opt-in, open data counties, in a common coordinate system. Users can join this dataset to the open parcel dataset using the objectid field to access parcel attributes in the standard GAC schema.
